other_conditions: The applicant must be a resident of Himachal Pradesh.
The applicant must be a Building/ Construction Worker.
The worker must have completed at least 90 days of building or other construction work in the last 12 months.
The worker’s registration with the Himachal Pradesh Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board must be renewed annually and remain active.
The worker’s wife must have delivered a baby to be eligible for the ₹6,000 benefit.
The worker must maintain proof of 90 days of work each year to retain eligibility for benefits.
benefits_summary: The scheme provides ₹6,000 to the worker’s wife for each delivery (up to two deliveries) and ₹1,000 to the male worker as paternity assistance on the birth of a child.
documents_required: Wage slip or appointment letter from the employer verifying 90 days of construction work
Certificate from a local authority (councilor, executive officer, or Panchayat Secretary) if wage slip/appointment letter is unavailable
Self‑attested copies of all mandatory documents
application_link: Step 1: Visit the Labor Welfare Office during office hours and request a hard copy of the prescribed application form. Step 2: Fill in all mandatory fields, paste a passport‑sized photograph (signed across if required), and attach self‑attested copies of all mandatory documents. Step 3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with a wage slip or appointment letter from the employer verifying 90 days of construction work; if unavailable, submit a certificate from a local authority (such as a councilor, executive officer, or Panchayat Secretary) to verify employment. Step 4: After submitting the documents and payment, receive an acknowledgment receipt confirming registration. Note: Ensure the application is submitted within the prescribed period, if any. After three years, visit the office to pay a renewal fee and submit proof of 90 days of work each year to maintain eligibility for benefits. A one‑time registration fee must be paid at the office, valid for three years.
